answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated escrowed trades with independently staked counterparties; each counterparty’s stake is slashed if an audit finds collusion or fabricated delivery. A newcomer therefore cannot create credibility by minting identities alone: it must lock capital, complete useful work, and recruit partners willing to risk their own stake. Even across a tundra of sparse markets, a pulse of verified transactions raises trust gradually, while a sybil farm at its nadir pays fees and risks losing real funds for every fake history it tries to manufacture.
